1 Scientific Literature.Title: Simulated Experiment Study of Factors Influencing the Hydration Activity of f-CaO in Basic Oxygen Furnace Slag
1 Scientific Literature.Journal_or_Source: Advances in Materials Science and Engineering, Vol. 2016, Article ID 7529382
1 Scientific Literature.Study_Objective: Reveal f-CaO composition in BOF slags and explain via simulated f-CaO why its hydration activity is low and how this drives volume expansion of cement containing BOF slag.
1 Scientific Literature.Abstract_or_Key_Finding: f-CaO in BOF slag includes calcium iron and calcium iron manganese phases (CaO-FeOx, CaO-FeOx-MnOy solid solutions). Hydration activity order: solid solutions < CaO in tricomponent f-CaO < monocomponent f-CaO. Calcination at 1600 °C restrains CaO hydration. Volume expansion rates of CaO, Ca2Fe2O5 and Ca3Fe1.5Mn1.5O8 are 97.88%, 43.44% and 52.02%; solid solutions hydrate slowly due to lower Gibbs-energy driving force, causing late expansion.
1 Scientific Literature.Notes: Motivated by BOF slag use in cement (CBS) but no binder/mortar tests.
